messages:
maria_s: starting POC with AcmeCorp — trying to wire up our log + trace export to their Datadog account. seeing a bunch of 429s when we hit the export endpoint and traces are arriving without trace_id attached. anyone seen this flow before?
ajohnson: can you paste the request headers from the export agent and a sample log line? 429 usually means rate limiting on our export egress or the customer's intake.
maria_s: paste below (redacted keys):
```
POST /v1/export HTTP/1.1
Host: exports.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-Request-Id: 8f7c1a
X-Traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
```
log sample: `{level: "info", msg: "inference request", trace_id: null, request_id: "8f7c1a"}`
ryan_dev: ok two things to check: 1) our export client must forward traceparent or x-redwood-trace-id into the downstream Datadog payload — looks like traceparent is present, but trace_id null in logs suggests our app lost it before logging. 2) 429s — check response headers for `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `Retry-After`. can you share the 429 response headers?
maria_s: 429 response looks like: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 15`
sales-eng: customers care about cost — if we bump export concurrency to avoid 429s, will that change billing for the POC?
ajohnson: it can increase egress/requests. short term workaround: batch exports and add a retry with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. also ensure sampling config on Datadog side isn't dropping traces because trace_id missing.
ajohnson: quick middleware fix (node express) to preserve trace id if missing: ```js
app.use((req,res,next)=>{
  req.headers['x-redwood-trace-id'] = req.headers['x-redwood-trace-id'] || req.headers['x-request-id'] || req.headers['x-traceparent']?.split('-')[1];
  next();
});
```
ryan_dev: for infra: we can flip the export traffic for AcmeCorp to the Dedicated pool for the POC (short window) to avoid shared-hosting rate caps. that requires a quick DNS/route change and temporary commit on their side. ops can rollback after demo.
maria_s: can we do that without a signed contract? they prefer trial — worried about auto-commits.
sales-eng: we can enable a temporary internal quota override for the trial org for 48h — track it manually. will need billing signoff, but lower risk than losing the deal.
deploy-bot: deploy started by ryan_dev: export-quota-override v1.2 -> staging
ajohnson: other thing — for Datadog, use the official trace id field in the trace payload (dd.trace_id) and map x-redwood-trace-id to it. If that's not possible, include trace id in the log message and configure the Datadog pipeline to correlate logs and traces by that field.
maria_s: doing the middleware change now and will enable batching + backoff. can someone run the temporary quota override for 24h while I validate?
ryan_dev: I can approve 24h. I'll ping finance and tag the change. after you validate, we'll roll back to default.
maria_s: thanks — will report back in ~45m with results. :pray:
